title: Finite scalar proper/open mate on strict reduction towers
statement:
Fix the finite-field datum of [def-pur-conventions], with algebraic closure $k$ of characteristic $p$, a prime $\ell\ne p$, and finite extensions $E\subset F$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$. Write $A=\mathcal O_E$, $B=\mathcal O_F$, $t=\varpi_E$, $v=\varpi_F$ and $e\geq1$ with $tB=v^eB$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $f:X\to Y$ be separated of finite type between separated finite-type $k$-schemes, and fix a compactification $c=(X\xrightarrow{j}\overline X\xrightarrow{p_c}Y)$ with $j$ open and $p_c$ proper [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties, def-weil-compactifications-refinements]. On the small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], put $R_W=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,W}$, $S_W=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{F,W}$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients] and $C_W=-\otimes^L_{R_W}S_W$ [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. Let $M\in D^b_{ctf}(X,\mathcal O_E)$, the derived-complete bounded constructible category with a uniform Tor-amplitude interval for all reductions [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed, def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude]. Write $A_n=A/t^n$, $B_n=B/t^nB=B/v^{en}$, $M_n=M\otimes^L_{R_X}(A_n)_X$, and $C_W^{(n)}=-\otimes^L_{(A_n)_W}(B_n)_W$. For $H=E,F$, let $P_H^c$ be the integral compact-support functor attached to $c$, defined as the total derived inverse limit of its finite separately derived proper/open images [def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support].

Use the strict reduction lifts $\mathcal T_E^c(M)$ and $\mathcal T_F^c(C_XM)$ of [lem-weil-compact-support-reduction-tower-functor], restricted to the discrete constant ring sheaves $\underline A$ and $\underline B$. A strict tower means a complex in $\operatorname{Fun}(\mathbf N_{\geq1}^{\mathrm{op}},\operatorname{Mod}(\underline A_W))$ or its $B$ analogue, with its ordinary derived category [def-weil-inverse-system, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. A superscript $(e)$ retains indices $en$ with composite transitions. Put $T=-\otimes_A B$ on constant-coefficient tower complexes; all finite coefficient objects are regarded as constant integral modules by restriction of scalars [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars].

For any level $n$, let $a_{p_c,n}:C_Y^{(n)}Rp_{c*,A_n}\to Rp_{c*,B_n}C_{\overline X}^{(n)}$ be the adjunction mate whose transpose at $N$ is $p_{c,B_n}^*C_Y^{(n)}Rp_{c*,A_n}N\cong C_{\overline X}^{(n)}p_{c,A_n}^*Rp_{c*,A_n}N\xrightarrow{C^{(n)}\varepsilon_{p_c,A_n}}C_{\overline X}^{(n)}N$, and let $b_{j,n}:C_{\overline X}^{(n)}j_!\to j_!C_X^{(n)}$ be the canonical extension-by-zero tensor map [def-weil-derived-direct-image, def-weil-extension-by-zero]. Denote their ordered composite by $q_{n,M}=Rp_{c*,B_n}(b_{j,n,M_n})\circ a_{p_c,n,j_!M_n}$.

There is a natural $B$-linear transformation in the derived category of strict towers
$$q_\bullet^c:T\mathcal T_E^c(M)\longrightarrow (\mathcal T_F^c(C_XM))^{(e)}.$$
It is the ordered composite of the proper scalar adjunction mate on the ringed diagram sites and the exact open coefficient tensor comparison, with replacements made in that diagram category. Under the canonical evaluated direct-image and coefficient-restriction identifications, its $n$-th evaluation is exactly $q_{n,M}$. Each $a_{p_c,n}$ and $b_{j,n}$, hence $q_{n,M}$ and $q_\bullet^c$, is invertible. On restriction of scalars, the first map is the canonical biproduct comparison for a finite $A_n$-basis of $B_n$; the second is ordinary extension-by-zero tensor balancing. The transformation is independent of the basis. Its quotient-transition squares commute in the derived strict-tower category, before taking any derived limit. Its proper/open factorization is the mate of the pasted pullback/coefficient square, with the canonical composite-adjunction normalization.

proof.text: Apply [lem-pur-compact-support-coefficient-models] to the given datum. Choose its single $A$-basis $b_1,\ldots,b_r$ of $B$; its reductions are bases of every $B_n$ over $A_n$. Retain the canonical constant/completed identifications of quotient diagrams and their transitions supplied there. Work on $J=\mathbf N_{\geq1}^{\mathrm{op}}$. By [lem-weil-pbc-diagram-site-realization] and [lem-pur-system-ringed-sequence-site], constant integral towers and the varying $A_n,B_n$ systems are module sheaves on small vertical diagram sites. All subsequent tensors, adjunctions and replacements are taken on these sites. In particular the finite-free constant sheaf $\underline B$ on the diagram site has the same basis at every index.

proof.text:
Let $D_E(M)$ be the strict derived reduction system before applying $j_!$ and $Rp_*$. On simultaneous K-flat representatives, tensor balancing gives a natural isomorphism of strict constant-$B$ towers
$$\kappa:T\operatorname{Res}_A D_E(M)\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Res}_B(D_F(C_XM))^{(e)}.$$
Indeed the component is $(P\otimes_A A_n)\otimes_A B\cong(P\otimes_A B)\otimes_B B/t^nB$, sending $(x\otimes\bar a)\otimes b$ to $(x\otimes b)\otimes\bar a$, with inverse $(x\otimes b)\otimes\bar c\mapsto(x\otimes1)\otimes b\bar c$. Here the expression on the right of the inverse is interpreted in $P\otimes_A B/t^nB$, so it is independent of lifts. These maps commute with each quotient. The completed-to-constant identification in [lem-pur-compact-support-coefficient-models] supplies this model of $C_XM$. The derived tensor and its actual system evaluations are supplied by [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections]; [lem-sfb-successive-derived-quotient-normalization] fixes the associators and unit. Thus this is an isomorphism on systems, natural in $M$, rather than a selection of maps in the individual fiber categories.

proof.text:
Use the specified geometric derived adjunctions on diagram sites from [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections]. For any strict constant-$A$ tower $N$ on $\overline X$, define $a^J_N:T_Y Rp^J_{*,A}N\to Rp^J_{*,B}T_{\overline X}N$ as the $p_B^*\dashv Rp^J_{*,B}$ adjunct of
$$p_B^*T_Y Rp^J_{*,A}N\xrightarrow{\mu}T_{\overline X}p_A^*Rp^J_{*,A}N\xrightarrow{T\varepsilon_A}T_{\overline X}N.$$
The balancing map $\mu$ is the pullback tensor comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-mate-exact], with the constant algebra pulled back from $Y$. Equivalently, under the scalar adjunction of [lem-pur-sheaf-ring-derived-coefficient-adjunction], this is the projection map with its $B$ action. The mate is formed in the $B$-module derived category, so it retains $B$-linearity. The counit formula makes it natural in the whole system $N$.

source.place: Tags 07A6, lemma-adjoint, and 0B56, equation-projection-formula-map, applied on the small diagram sites

proof.text: The proper map just constructed is invertible. Apply the coefficient-restriction comparison of [lem-pur-diagram-ring-restriction-pushforward]. It identifies its restricted target with $Rp^J_{*,A}\operatorname{Res}_A T N$. By [lem-pur-finite-free-scalar-extension], tensor by $B$ has the finite direct-sum coordinates $\operatorname{Res}_A T N\cong N^{\oplus r}$, also on complexes and towers. If $\iota_i:N\to N^{\oplus r}$ is inclusion, the transpose of the $i$th column of the restricted $a^J$ is $\iota_i\varepsilon_N$: balancing sends $x\otimes b_i$ to that same basis column. The adjunction triangle identity therefore identifies the column with $Rp^J_{*,A}(\iota_i)$. Consequently the restricted map is the canonical biproduct comparison. Its inverse has components $Rp^J_{*,A}(\pi_i)$: the equations $\pi_i\iota_j=\delta_{ij}$ and $\sum_i\iota_i\pi_i=1$ remain true under this additive derived functor. Restriction reflects isomorphisms here directly: it changes neither underlying complexes nor their cohomology; the cone of a map has zero cohomology if its restriction does. This proves invertibility in $D(B)$ on the diagram site, not merely after evaluation. The same argument with rings $A_n,B_n$ proves invertibility of every finite proper mate. D4 stage-3 implementation: factors_isIso uses the existing proper_biproduct and strictProper_biproduct identities. Choose the integral basis constructed in [lem-weil-completed-integral-finite-free]. The constant sheaf basis construction of [lem-pur-constant-finite-free-section-basis] gives its sheaf basis. For the finite quotients, the ramification equality identifies the target ideal with the image of the source ideal; quotient the same basis using [lem-pur-adic-basis-limit] and sheafify. Exact conservative restriction reflects derived isomorphisms by the homology-functor comparison and the cohomological isomorphism criterion. In each biproduct identity, every factor following the restricted proper mate is an isomorphism: the normalized restriction square, direct image of the coordinate isomorphism, and the product comparison of a right adjoint. Cancel these factors and reflect the resulting isomorphism. For the open factors use openTensor_ordinary and open_base_ordinary, with the finite basis pulled back to the compactification space. These are whole-tower arguments; no conservativity of evaluated derived tower functors is assumed. The two biproduct identities remain named obligations of this same node, rather than new split statements. F8 basis-transport implementation: pull back the given target basis using the geometric module inverse-image functor. Its product comparison identifies the pullback of the finite power of the regular module with the finite power on the source. The adjunct of the structural ring map on regular modules is invertible: compare the specified adjunction with Mathlib's module pullback adjunction by leftAdjointUniq, and use pullbackObjUnitToUnit. Compose the pullback of the target basis with the existing restriction/pullback isomorphism and this regular-module isomorphism. The inverse-mate unit identity identifies the adjunct of that composite with restriction of the structural ring map followed by the identity-on-sections direct-image comparison. The finite-product projection equations then give exactly the sectionwise formula in pulledBasis_existsUnique. For uniqueness, transpose the coordinate equations, cancel the same invertible regular-module comparison, and use product extensionality to identify the inverse basis maps. This proves the existing basis-transport obligation without any new existence assumption or hole. The remaining finite biproduct identities are reduced by product extensionality to the two coordinate statements of the split nodes.

source.place: Tags 0B56, equation-projection-formula-map, and 0944, lemma-projection-formula, finite-free case

proof.text: On the same diagram sites take the canonical open scalar map $b^J:T_{\overline X}j_!\to j_!T_X$. The identity-base-change coefficient case of [lem-sf-open-tensor-normalization] supplies this invertible derived map on arbitrary strict systems and fixes its open-adjunction normalization. In the present finite-free situation it is already ordinary tensor balancing: [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-slice-extension-tensor] identifies extension by zero and tensor; on the open a tensor $x\otimes b$ is unchanged, and extension by zero carries its zero sections to zero. Exact open extension is supplied by [lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact]. Thus localization gives precisely the stated derived open comparison. The same construction for $A_n\to B_n$ gives $b_{j,n}$, also invertible. The ordinary base-site invertibility admits a shorter categorical verification: the specified open restriction map is the inverse mate of the pullback/restriction isomorphism under the open adjunctions. Taking its inverse mate under the scalar adjunctions is therefore inverse conjugation of that isomorphism under the two composite adjunctions. Conjugation preserves isomorphisms [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-conjugate]. This proves ordinaryBaseOpenTensor_isIso without a new sectionwise tensor construction. The tower map ordinaryOpenTensor is the postcomposition image of ordinaryBaseOpenTensor, as is checked on each module and tower index. Hence ordinaryOpenTensor_isIso follows because functors preserve isomorphisms. For openTensor_ordinary, use the proved exactDerivedMate unit equation from [def-sp-varying-ring-operations]. The exact derived adjunction equals the right-derived scalar adjunction transported along its canonical exactness isomorphism: their units agree on the homotopy-category localization, by the derived-unit factorization. Injectivity of the scalar hom equivalence then identifies the inverse mate with the localized ordinary isomorphism. For open_base_ordinary, finiteScalar_exact gives exactness in the chosen target basis and its pulled source basis. Apply the same exactDerivedMate equation on the base sites, and transport the two scalar left adjoints to pbcDerivedExtend using leftAdjointUniq. The unit identity for leftAdjointUniq and naturality of the restriction square show that inverse mating commutes with this transport. The result is exactly baseOpenExactNormalization, including its specified universal-adjunction normalizations. For the generic iterated-mate isomorphism, simplify the TwoSquare/equivalence projections and apply Mathlib conjugateEquiv_symm_iso directly. This keeps the adjunction structures folded during elaboration. The common localization/unit calculation is factored into the proved private helper localizedInverseMate_eq, shared by both open normalization proofs, so it is checked generically rather than repeatedly unfolding the geometric coefficient data.

source.place: Tag 0E8I, lemma-j-shriek-and-tensor; exact open extension, Tag 03DJ

proof.text:
Identify the restricted compact-support lift with the separately derived proper image of exact open extension on the constant towers. This is the construction specified in [lem-weil-compact-support-reduction-tower-functor]; the passage from its native varying-ring system to constant towers is [lem-pur-diagram-ring-restriction-pushforward], and open restriction is the literal sheafified extension with the same action. Selecting the $F$ indices $en$ commutes with this calculation. For completeness, on constant towers the selection functor has exact left adjoint: at index $m$ it assigns $K_{\lceil m/e\rceil}$, with the evident block transitions. Its adjunction follows because a map out of that block is determined by the map at its last index $en$ and the target transitions. By [lem-weil-pbc-right-adjoint-preserves-kinjective], selection preserves K-injectives. Hence selecting a simultaneous K-injective representative computes the separately derived proper image of the selected constant tower; termwise open extension commutes with selection literally. No claim about K-injectivity of varying-ring evaluations is needed. Apply this identification and $\kappa$ of Step 2 to define
$$q^c_\bullet=Rp^J_{*,B}j_!(\kappa)\circ Rp^J_{*,B}(b^J)\circ a^J_{j_!D_E(M)}.$$
Its endpoints are exactly $T\mathcal T_E^c(M)$ and $(\mathcal T_F^c(C_XM))^{(e)}$. All three factors are natural $B$-linear isomorphisms, so the composite is such an isomorphism. In Lean, subsequence_preservesKInjective applies the existing restriction_preservesKInjectives lemma from [lem-sp-strict-tower-arithmetic-restriction-resolution] to the actual arithmetic index functor, so no new choice of resolutions is needed.

proof.text: Check the actual evaluated arrow. [lem-weil-pbc-tower-derived-evaluation-normalization] identifies evaluation of the constant-tower proper adjunction, including its counit, with the ambient one. [lem-pur-system-evaluation-scalar-restriction-normalization] identifies that comparison with the singleton-derived evaluation of the varying coefficient system, including the coefficient-restriction isomorphism. Its counit identity ensures that the evaluated transpose is exactly $p_{B_n}^*C_Y^{(n)}Rp_{*,A_n}N\cong C_{\overline X}^{(n)}p_{A_n}^*Rp_{*,A_n}N\to C_{\overline X}^{(n)}N$. Tensor/reduction identification uses the balancing of Step 2, and the normalized scalar unit is $x\mapsto x\otimes1$ by [lem-pur-sheaf-ring-derived-coefficient-adjunction]. Thus the proper factor evaluates to the specified $a_{p_c,n}$ as a finite-$B_n$ arrow under coefficient restriction, not an unspecified map between its endpoints. The open factor evaluates to $b_{j,n}$ by its open-unit normalization [lem-sf-open-tensor-normalization]. Functoriality now gives the ordered composite $Rp_{c*,B_n}(b_{j,n,M_n})\circ a_{p_c,n,j_!M_n}$, namely $q_{n,M}$. J1 stage-3 refinement: evaluationRestriction_existsUnique first uses coefficientSequenceRestriction_evaluation, then postcomposes with constant restriction. The resulting equality of functors gives the identity-on-sections isomorphism; sectionwise extensionality proves uniqueness. Finite derived balancing needs no new basis construction: the stated ordinary finite balancing identifies finite scalar extension followed by positive restriction with finite restriction followed by exact constant tensor. Positive restriction is exact and conservative, so finite scalar extension is exact. Its canonical universal left-derived counit is therefore invertible. Localize the ordinary balancing and transport through that counit and the exact localization factors. The localization universal property gives exactly the cochain-counit equation and uniqueness of finiteBalancing_existsUnique. Conservativity of a composite restriction is proved on each morphism: its image in the underlying sheaf category is the image of the twice-restricted morphism. Mapping an isomorphism through the underlying-sheaf functor and reflecting there proves the assertion. The generic identity-on-sections helper accepts an explicit family of section types and equality with the evaluated carriers. These carrier equalities are checked by unfolding only restriction and evaluation, avoiding equality tests between complete module structures. This preserves exactly the original identity-on-sections characterization. Q6 stage-3 refinement: finiteOrdinaryBalancing_existsUnique now assembles the individual finite quotient module isomorphisms of [lem-pur-finite-quotient-module-balancing]. Naturality is proved, rather than assumed: injectivity of the constant scalar adjunction hom equivalence reduces it to 1 tensor x; naturality of the two tensor units and the normalized component formula give the square. The same injectivity proves uniqueness of the natural isomorphism. Thus the remaining single-module tensor/quotient construction has no naturality or uniqueness obligation. C1: The already proved constructions through targetEvaluation are relocated verbatim to [def-pur-strict-scalar-mate-evaluation-data] to make the finite normalization obligation independently importable. The exact evaluated-arrow equation is [lem-pur-strict-scalar-mate-finite-evaluation], asserting only this step, without invertibility or transition clauses.

source.place: Tags 07A6, lemma-adjoint, and 0940, section-derived-limits; singleton/counit normalization rather than faithfulness of derived evaluation

proof.text: The construction used no basis until its invertibility test in Step 4; adjunction and the canonical balancing maps therefore make $q^c_\bullet$ independent of that choice. Quotient compatibility is an equation of the constructed system transformations. In Step 2 the quotient maps commute on representatives, since both composites take $(x\otimes b)$ to $x\otimes\bar b$. For the proper factor, use the unit/counit and transition compatibility in [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections] and [lem-pur-system-evaluation-scalar-restriction-normalization]; applying the natural Hom bijection to the commuting pullback/tensor square gives the commuting mate square. For the open factor use the actual-system open map of [lem-sf-open-tensor-normalization]. Pasting gives all quotient-transition squares before any limit. For the factorization use the scalar adjunctions $T\dashv\operatorname{Res}$ on $X,\overline X,Y$. The $T\dashv\operatorname{Res}$ mate of the restriction square $\delta$ of [lem-pur-diagram-ring-restriction-pushforward] has adjunct $Rp^J_{*,A}(\eta_N)$, $\eta(x)=x\otimes1$; on the $i$th summand it is $Rp^J_{*,A}(\iota_i)$, which is the column of $a^J$ computed in Step 4. Two $B$-maps out of $T(-)$ with equal adjuncts are equal, so $a^J$ is this mate. Likewise $b^J$ is the mate of $\operatorname{Res}j_!=j_!\operatorname{Res}$, since both send $x\otimes b$ to $x\otimes b$. Clause (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting], with $\alpha=b^J$, $\beta=a^J$, $G,H=j_!$ and $G_2,H_2=Rp^J_*$, identifies the ordered composite $Rp^J_{*,B}(b^J)\circ a^J_{j_!}$ with the mate of the pasted restriction square $Rp^J_{*,A}j_!\operatorname{Res}\cong\operatorname{Res}Rp^J_{*,B}j_!$ for the composite functor $Rp_*j_!$. Clause (2) is not used, since $j_!$ is a left adjoint. These equations are obtained in the diagram derived categories themselves; no inference that evaluated maps detect equality is made. The Lean arrow_transition theorem is exactly naturality of diagramTransition at the whole-diagram arrow. The two geometric transpose theorems are obtained categorically: the inverse of normalized left-adjoint uniqueness is inverse conjugation of the restriction square; iterated mate/conjugation and the mate-counit identity give the stated geometric transpose. The Lean comparison_pasted applies mateEquiv_vcomp to the open and proper scalar mates and uses the inverse bijection. The auxiliary restriction exactness assertions follow by composing exact restrictions; baseTensor_exact is a retract of exact tower tensor via constant diagrams and evaluation at index zero. These arguments change no definition or statement. Finite quotient evaluation and biproduct assertions, and the final assembly theorem, remain the original named Lean obligations.
